requirements.evidence: Every contract item is present: app/Models/Entity.php:22 returns 'slug' (route key), :48 owner() query; app/Models/EntityMembership.php:13/24/32-54 enum cast + owner/admin/employee scopes; app/Models/UserRole.php:6-16; app/Models/User.php:38-54 memberships/entities/membershipFor; migrations define `entities_slug_unique`, cascade FKs, role default 'employee', `entity_memberships_entity_user_unique`, `owner_seq` storedAs (database/migrations/2026_10_29_064555_create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-25); both policies implement every rule (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:14-40, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-41); factories include owner/admin/employee states; docs/database-schema.md is updated. Edge cases (second owner rejected, one owner per entity, unlimited non-owners) are tested.

conventions.evidence: Follows the applicable conventions: generated-style migrations with reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_064554_create_entities_table.php:26-29), `#[Fillable]` matching the existing User model style (app/Models/Entity.php:13, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:13), authorization in policies, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md kept in sync. Small deviation: `User::membershipFor()` (app/Models/User.php:51) and `EntityMembership::isOwner()` (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:72) are public methods without the PHPDoc the conventions ask for.

security.evidence: All authorization is server-side in app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:14-40 and app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-41, resolved through membership lookups; non-members are denied (EntityMembershipPolicyTest crosses entities), the owner membership is never deletable (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:25-30), self-removal is the only special case. Mass assignment is restricted via `#[Fillable(['name', 'slug'])` and `#[Fillable(['entity_id', 'user_id', 'role'])`; there are no views/unescaped output or secrets. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: Tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php covers factories, route key, soft deletes, enum, scopes, relations, DB default role, both unique constraints, owner_seq generation and named indexes; tests/Feature/EntityPolicyTest.php covers every policy outcome including non-members and another entity's owner. Gap: the `user_id` cascade is never exercised (tests/Feature/EntityModelTest.php:146 deletes only the entity).

simplicity.evidence: Lean models/policies that reuse `membershipFor()` and the DB constraint; no service/repository layer. Only extra is the unused `EntityMembership::isOwner()` helper (app/Models/EntityMembership.php:72-75), which nothing calls (policies compare `role` directly).

readability.evidence: Clear names, generic PHPDoc on relations and scopes (app/Models/Entity.php:57-77, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:29-50), small focused policy methods, consistent with the sibling User model; no debug output or duplicated logic.

scope.evidence: The diff only adds the two migrations, Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole, factories, both policies, their tests, the schema doc and changelog entry; no routes, Livewire components, session handling, onboarding or other out-of-scope work.

issues.explanation: Only the entity→membership cascade is tested; there is no test that deletes a user to prove the `user_id` cascade required by the task.
`membershipFor()` (and `EntityMembership::isOwner()` at app/Models/EntityMembership.php:72) lack the PHPDoc that the conventions require on public methods touched.
`isOwner()` is unused dead code; the policies compare `role` directly, so the helper only adds surface area.

review.summary: Implements the complete tenant persistence layer — migrations with a portable database-enforced single owner, Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole, factories, both policies, a thorough Pest suite and synced schema/changelog docs. Requirements and security are fully covered; only minor gaps (untested user-delete cascade, an unused helper, two missing PHPDoc blocks) keep it at approve-with-nits.
